hints.title: Frequency Sorting
hints.text: Letters that appear most frequently should require the fewest keypresses.

hints.title: Key Capacity Distribution
hints.text: There are 9 keys. The top 9 frequent letters need 1 press each, the next 9 need 2 presses each, and the rest need 3.

hints.title: Assigning Multipliers by Rank
hints.text: For the i-th most frequent character (0-indexed), its press cost is (i // 9) + 1.

hints.title: Greedy Frequency Assignment Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def minimumKeypresses(self, s: str) -> int:
        counts = sorted(Counter(s).values(), reverse=True)
        total = 0
        for i, cnt in enumerate(counts):
            cost = (i // 9) + 1
            total += cnt * cost
        return total
```

complexity.notes: Sorting at most 26 letter frequencies takes constant time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Assigning letters without sorting by frequency leads to suboptimal keypress combinations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Frequency table stores up to 26 character counts.
